subject: Animation
title: Hanna-Barbera's Limited Animation
description: A micro-lesson that makes Hanna-Barbera's Limited Animation usable.

hook.text: Hanna-Barbera needed to produce cartoons cheaply for TV, so they invented limited animation techniques.

buildup.text: They reused backgrounds, kept characters mostly still, and only animated mouths and arms when necessary.

discovery.text: This cut costs by over 90 percent compared to the full animation used in theatrical Disney films.

twist.text: Critics hated the cheap look. Audiences loved the characters anyway. Story trumped visual polish.

climax.text: Limited animation made TV cartoons economically viable and created an entire industry.

punchline.text: Cutting corners on animation built a cartoon empire.

quiz.question: Why did Hanna-Barbera develop limited animation techniques?
options: To create a unique artistic style
To reduce costs by over 90 percent, making TV cartoon production economically viable
To speed up film production for theatrical release
